```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
# show an sstable as a markdown table: the two header rows become the column names
show_table <- function(tab, rows = NULL) {
  m <- as.matrix(tab)
  body <- m[-(1:2), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!is.null(rows)) body <- body[rows, , drop = FALSE]
  knitr::kable(body, col.names = trimws(paste(m[1, ], m[2, ])), row.names = FALSE)
}
```

# C306

C306 collects the R tools used by the Biostatistics group of the Oxford
University Clinical Research Unit (OUCRU) to analyse and report clinical
studies:

- **report tables**: baseline characteristics, adverse events, and time-to-event
  comparisons (Cox, Fine–Gray, restricted mean survival time, cumulative
  incidence), overall and by subgroup, as flextables (Word, HTML, PDF) or
  plain matrices;
- **model summaries**: odds ratios with likelihood-ratio or Wald CIs, also
  within subgroups of an interacting variable;
- **plots**: Aalen–Johansen curves for competing risks, Box–Cox profile
  likelihood;
- **data tools**: import an OUCRU data dictionary, format raw data with it, and
  check the data for missing and out-of-range values.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("oucru-biostats/C306")
```

## Quick start

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(C306)
library(survival)

bl <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "baseline_data.csv", package = "C306"))
```

**Baseline table.** Each row variable is summarised by arm: continuous variables
with the statistics you ask for, categorical variables as n (%).

```{r}
tab <- sstable.baseline(age + sex + icudays ~ Arm, data = bl,
                        statistics = "median (Q1-Q3)", test = TRUE)
show_table(tab$table)
```

Add `flextable = TRUE` (or call `ss_flextable(tab)`) for a formatted table that
can be saved with `flextable::save_as_docx()`.

**Adverse events.** Number of episodes and of patients with at least one event,
by arm:

```{r}
ae <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "ae_data.csv", package = "C306"))
tab <- sstable.ae(ae_data = ae, fullid_data = bl, id.var = "usubjid",
                  aetype.var = "ctcaename", grade.var = "ctcaegrade",
                  arm.var = "Arm", flextable = FALSE)
show_table(tab$table, rows = 1:6)
```

**Time to event.** Events, absolute risk, hazard ratio and median survival:

```{r}
lung2 <- transform(na.omit(lung[, c("time", "status", "sex")]),
                   arm = factor(sex, labels = c("Male", "Female")))
tab <- sstable.survcomp(Surv(time, status) ~ arm, data = lung2, flextable = FALSE)
show_table(tab$table)
```

Use `compare.method = "rmst"` for a restricted mean survival time comparison,
`sstable.survcomp.subgroup()` for subgroup analyses, and a competing-risks
outcome (`Surv(time, event)` with a factor `event`) for Fine–Gray models.

## Main functions

| Area | Functions |
|---|---|
| Report tables | `sstable.baseline()`, `sstable.ae()`, `sstable.survcomp()`, `sstable.survcomp.subgroup()` |
| Formatting tables | `ss_flextable()`, `ss_huxtable()`, `as_sstable()`, `ss_format()`, `ft_sstheme()`, `ht_theme_markdown()`, `ht_theme_kable()`, `rbind()` |
| Models | `logist_summary()`, `subgroup_effect()`, `explicit()` |
| Plots | `gg_ajsurvplot()`, `gg_ajsurvplot2()`, `ggsurvfit2()`, `tidy_survfit2()`, `gg_boxcox()` |
| Data tools | `import.info()`, `convert.info()`, `myformat.data()`, `inspect.data()`, `getlabel()`, `labAE()`, `createProject()` |
| Helpers | `contSummary()`, `pct()`, `simple_recode()`, `simple_relevel()`, `simple_sort()`, `ref_lv()`, `mutate_f()`, `summarise_f()` |

See `vignette("C306_vignette_v6", package = "C306")` for a detailed guide to the
report tables, and `NEWS.md` for changes, including the **impact of fixed bugs on
previous reports**.

## Authors
